           PENDING              │\n│  container.start          PENDING/STOPPED   STARTING             │\n│  health_status: healthy   STARTING          RUNNING              │\n│  health_status: unhealthy RUNNING           UNHEALTHY*           │\n│  health_status: healthy   UNHEALTHY*        RUNNING              │\n│  container.stop           RUNNING/STARTING  STOPPING → STOPPED   │\n│  container.die            (any)             DEAD                 │\n│  container.start          DEAD              STARTING (restart)   │\n│  container.oom            (any)             DEAD             │\n│  * UNHEALTHY is a health_state, not lifecycle_state.            │\n│    lifecycle_state stays RUNNING during health failures.         │\n│    lifecycle_state = DEAD only on container.die or oom.          │\n│                                                                  │\n│  DIAGRAM:                                                        │\n│ start   ┌──────────┐          │              │\n│       │PENDING ├─────────►│ STARTING ├──────────┤              │\n│       └────────┘          └────┬─────┘          │              │\n│                                │ healthy        │              │\n│                                ▼                │              │\n│  unpause    ┌─────────────────────────────┐     │              │\n│ │\n│    pause       │ stop   │ die       │ unhealthy  │              │\n│       ┌────────┘        │           │   (lifecycle              │\n│       ▼                 ▼           │    stays RUNNING)         │\n│  ┌─────────┐        ┌───────┐      │              │              │\n│  │ STOPPED │◄───────┤ DEAD  │◄─────┘              │              │\n│  └─────────┘        └───┬───┘                     │              │\n│                         │ start                    │              │\n│                         └──────────────────────────┘              │\n│ FAILURE HANDLING STRATEGY\n\n### 4.1 Failure Mode Matrix\n\n```\n┌──────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│ Failure                  │ Strategy                                        │\n├──────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│ Docker socket unreachable│ Circuit breaker + exponential backoff           │\n│                          │ CP keeps serving cached state                    │\n│                          │ Reconnects automatically (max 30s delay)        │\n├──────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│ Docker socket reset      │ Auto-reconnect (next read attempt)              │\n│ (daemon restart)         │ Full reconciliation on reconnect                 │\n│                          │ Events during downtime = missed (see below)     │\n├──────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│ Event stream timeout     │ Reset stream, reconnect                         │\n│                          │ Docker events stream doesn't have native timeout│\n│                          │ Watchdog detects silence > 60s → force reconnect│\n├──────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│ Queue full               │ Backpressure: drop oldest event                 │\n│ (consumer too slow)      │ Log dropped events                              │\n│                          │ Increase queue size if persistent               │\n├──────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│ Event processing error   │ Log error, skip event, continue                 │\n│ (transform fails)        │ Don't block the queue                           │\n│                          │ Track error count for alerting                   │\n├──────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│ Registry update fails    │ Log error, event still dispatched to bus        │\n│ (DB down)                │ Registry reconciles on next sync cycle          │\n├──────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│ Circuit breaker OPEN     │ Stop attempting connections                     │\n│                          │ CP serves stale cache (5s TTL)                  │\n│                          │ After recovery_timeout: HALF_OPEN → retry       │\n├──────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│ Missed events            │ Reconciliation Loop detects drift               │\n│ (during downtime)        │ Compares Docker state vs Registry state         │\n│                          │ Registers/deregisters to match reality          │\n└──────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\n### 4.2 Missed Events Recovery\n\n```\n  Time ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────►\n\n  Docker Engine:    ──[event]──[event]──[DOWN]──[event]──[event]──\n                                    │                  │\n  CP Listener:      ──[event]──[event]──[DISCONNECT]──[RECONNECT]\n                                            │              │\n  Events missed:                           │              │\n  container.died ─────────────────────────────────────────► DETECTED\n  container.start ─────────────────────────────────────────► DETECTED\n                                                           │\n  Reconciliation Loop:                  ────[SYNC]─────────► FIX\n                                                           │\n  Registry:                             ────[UPDATE]───────► MATCH\n```\n\n### 4.3 Graceful Degradation\n\n```python\nclass GracefulDegradation:\n    \"\"\"\n    When Docker socket is unreachable, the Control Plane continues\n    to serve existing state with degraded freshness guarantees.\n    \"\"\"\n    \n    STALENESS_LEVELS = {\n        \"fresh\":    timedelta(seconds=10),    # Last event < 10s ago\n        \"recent\":   timedelta(seconds=60),    # Last event < 60s ago\n        \"stale\":    timedelta(seconds=300),   # Last event < 5min ago\n        \"unknown\":  timedelta(seconds=600),   # Last event > 10min ago\n    }\n    \n    def assess_freshness(self, last_event_at: datetime) -> str:\n        age = datetime.utcnow() - last_event_at\n        for level, threshold in reversed(list(self.STALENESS_LEVELS.items())):\n            if age >= threshold:\n                return level\n        return \"fresh\"\n    \n    def get_api_response_headers(self, freshness: str) -> dict:\n        return {\n            \"X-Registry-Freshness\": freshness,\n            \"X-Registry-Warning\": (\n                \"Data may be stale\" if freshness in (\"stale\", \"unknown\") else None\n            ),\n        }\n```\n\n---\n\n## 5. OBSERVABILITY\n\n### 5.1 Metrics (Prometheus)\n\n```\n# Listener health\nosiris_listener_connected{state=\"connected|disconnected|reconnecting\"} 1\nosiris_listener_events_received_total{source=\"docker\"} 12345\nosiris_listener_events_processed_total{type=\"container.started\"} 6789\nosiris_listener_events_dropped_total{reason=\"queue_full\"} 42\nosiris_listener_events_errors_total{type=\"transform_error\"} 3\nosiris_listener_queue_size 15\nosiris_listener_reconnect_attempts_total 7\nosiris_listener_last_event_timestamp_seconds 1686931200\n\n# Circuit breaker\nosiris_circuit_breaker_state{state=\"closed|open|half_open\"} 1\nosiris_circuit_breaker_failures_total 12\n```\n\n### 5.2 Structured Logging\n\n```python\n# Every event processed gets a structured log line\nlogger.info(\n    \"Event processed\",\n    extra={\n        \"event_id\": event.event_id,\n        \"service_id\": event.service_id,\n        \"event_type\": event.event_type.value,\n        \"severity\": event.severity.value,\n        \"processing_time_ms\": elapsed_ms,\n        \"queue_depth\": queue_size,\n    }\n)\n\n# Connection state changes\nlogger.warning(\n    \"Connection state changed\",\n    extra={\n        \"old_state\": \"connected\",\n        \"new_state\": \"disconnected\",\n        \"reason\": \"ConnectionResetError\",\n        \"attempt\": reconnect_attempt,\n        \"next_retry_seconds\": delay,\n    }\n)\n```\n\n---\n\n## 6. CONFIGURATION\n\n```yaml\n# In config/platform.yaml → config_management section\nevent_listener:\n  enabled: true\n  max_queue_size: 1000\n  observed_actions:\n    - create\n    - start\n    - stop\n    - die\n    - kill\n    - oom\n    - pause\n    - unpause\n    - \"health_status: healthy\"\n    - \"health_status: unhealthy\"\n    - \"health_status: starting\"\n  reconnect:\n    base_delay_ms: 1000\n    max_delay_ms: 30000\n    multiplier: 2.0\n  circuit_breaker:\n    failure_threshold: 5\n    recovery_timeout_s: 30\n  watchdog:\n    interval_s: 30\n    max_silence_s: 60\n  enrichment:\n    inspect_on_start: true\n    inspect_on_health_change: false\n```\n\n---\n\n*This document defines the Docker Event Listener service. See also `SERVICE_REGISTRY_DESIGN.md`, `CONTROL_PLANE_ARCHITECTURE.md`.*","operationIsLocatedInWorkspace":true,"startLineNumbers":[]}

### Tour 1945 — Assistant

*2026-06-16 13:01:59 UTC*

Docker Event Listener service conçu et documenté dans `DOCKER_EVENT_LISTENER_DESIGN.md`.

**Architecture (6 composants) :**
1. **Connection Manager** — Socket pool docker-py + Reconnect Manager (exp backoff, max 30s) + Circuit Breaker (closed→half_open→open)
2. **Event Stream Reader** — Stream Docker GET /events → bounded queue (max 1000) avec backpressure (drop oldest)
3. **Event Transformer** — Pipeline Raw → Extract → Enrich (container inspect + registry lookup) → Classify → Normalize
4. **Event Bus** — Dispatch async vers subscribers (Registry, Health Monitor, Event Store)
5. **Registry Updater** — Applique les transitions d'état (lifecycle + health) via UPSERT
6. **Health Watchdog** — Surveille la santé du listener (silence detection > 60s → force reconnect)

**Pseudo-code complet pour 5 classes :**
- `DockerEventListener` — Main class avec 3 loops async (read, process, watchdog)
- `EventTransformer` — 6 étapes de transformation avec action mapping table (12 Docker actions → PlatformEvents)
- `ReconnectManager` — Exponential backoff avec jitter
- `CircuitBreaker` — 3 états (closed/open/half_open) avec recovery timeout
- `RegistryUpdater` — State machine maps (lifecycle + health transitions)

**Event Transformation Schema :**
- Input : Raw Docker event JSON
- Output : Normalized PlatformEvent (event_id, service_id, event_type, severity, payload enrichi)
- Classification matrix complète : 15 Docker actions → event types avec severity et registry update

**State Machine :**
- 7 lifecycle states (PENDING→STARTING→RUNNING→STOPPED→DEAD)
- 6 health states
- Transitions documentées avec diagramme complet
- Note importante : UNHEALTHY est un health_state, pas un lifecycle_state

**Failure Handling (8 modes) :**
- Socket unreachable → Circuit breaker + backoff
- Socket reset → Auto-reconnect + reconciliation
- Queue full → Backpressure drop oldest
- Missed events → Reconciliation Loop détecte le drift
- Graceful degradation → 4 niveaux de fraîcheur (fresh/recent/stale/unknown) avec headers HTTP

**Observabilité :** 8 métriques Prometheus + logging structuré
**Configuration :** YAML intégré dans platform.yamlHAS_CHANGES

API DESIGN PRINCIPLES\n\n| Principle | Implementation |\n|---|---|\n| **RESTful** | Resource-oriented URLs, HTTP methods map to CRUD + actions |\n| **Real-time state** | Every GET reflects live state from Service Registry (no stale cache > 5s) |\n| **Idempotent mutations** | POST /start on already-running service = 200 OK (no-op) |\n| **Consistent errors** | RFC 7807 Problem Details format for all error responses |\n| **Future WebSocket** | All list endpoints support `?stream=true` for SSE/WebSocket upgrade |\n| **Auth-ready** | Middleware slot for JWT/API key, currently passthrough in dev |\n\n---\n\n## 2. API SURFACE\n\n### 2.1 Base Configuration\n\n```\nBase URL:       http://[REDACTED:PASSWORD]@app.middleware(\"http\")\nasync def auth_passthrough(request: Request, call_next):\n    # Dev mode: pass through\n    # Production: validate token\n    return await call_next(request)\n```\n\n### 5.2 Phase 2: JWT + API Key\n\n```python\n# Two authentication methods:\n# 1. JWT Bearer token (for web UI)\n# 2. API Key header (for CLI, scripts, services)\n\n@app.middleware(\"http\")\nasync def auth_middleware(request: Request, call_next):\n    # Skip auth for health endpoints\n    if request.url.path in (\"/health\", \"/ready\", \"/docs\", \"/openapi.json\"):\n        return await call_next(request)\n    \n    # Check Authorization header\n    auth_header = request.headers.get(\"Authorization\", \"\")\n    \n    if auth_header.startswith(\"Bearer \"):\n        [REDACTED:ENV_VAR]        payload = verify_jwt(token)\n        request.state.user = payload[\"sub\"]\n        request.state.role = payload.get(\"role\", \"viewer\")\n        \n    elif request.headers.get(\"X-API-Key\"):\n        [REDACTED:ENV_VAR]        user = verify_api_key(api_key)\n        request.state.user = user.id\n        request.state.role = user.role\n        \n    else:\n        raise HTTPException(401, \"Missing authentication\")\n    \n    # Role-based access control\n    if request.method in (\"POST\", \"PUT\", \"DELETE\"):\n        if request.state.role not in (\"admin\", \"operator\"):\n            raise HTTPException(403, \"Insufficient permissions\")\n    \n    return await call_next(request)\n```\n\n### 5.3 Role Definitions\n\n```\n┌──────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│ Role         │ Permissions                                     │\n├──────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│ viewer       │ GET /services, GET /health, GET /graph          │\n│ operator     │ + POST /start, /stop, /restart                  │\n│ admin        │ + DELETE /services, config mutations, auth mgmt  │\n│ service      │ Internal services (JWT with service identity)    │\n└──────────────┴─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\n---\n\n## 6. RATE LIMITING\n\n```yaml\nrate_limits:\n  # Per role\n  viewer:\n    requests_per_minute: 120\n    burst: 20\n  operator:\n    requests_per_minute: 60\n    burst: 10\n  admin:\n    requests_per_minute: 300\n    burst: 50\n  \n  # Per endpoint\n  lifecycle_actions:\n    requests_per_minute: 10   # POST /start, /stop, /restart\n    burst: 3\n  \n  # Global\n  global:\n    requests_per_minute: 1000\n    burst: 200\n```\n\n---\n\n## 7. FUTURE WebSocket UPGRADE PATH\n\n### Current (v1): SSE\n\n```\nGET /api/v1/events?stream=true\n→ Content-Type: text/event-stream\n→ Server-Sent Events (unidirectional)\n```\n\n### Future (v2): WebSocket\n\n```\nWS /api/v1/ws/events\n→ Bidirectional communication\n→ Client can subscribe/unsubscribe\n→ Client can send commands\n→ Heartbeat/ping-pong\n```\n\n### Upgrade Header (v1 → v2 migration)\n\n```\n# Server advertises WebSocket support\nGET /api/v1/events\nResponse Headers:\n  Upgrade: websocket\n  X-WebSocket-URL: ws://host:8100/api/v1/ws/events\n```\n\n---\n\n## 8. RESPONSE HEADERS\n\nEvery response includes these standard headers:\n\n```\nX-Request-Id:         req_abc123def456        # Tracing\nX-Api-Version:        1.0.0                   # API version\nX-Registry-Freshness: fresh|recent|stale      # Data freshness\nX-Rate-Limit-Remaining: 119                   # Rate limit remaining\nX-Rate-Limit-Reset:   1686931260              # Rate limit reset (epoch)\n```\n\n---\n\n*This document defines the Control Plane REST API. See also `CONTROL_PLANE_ARCHITECTURE.md`, `SERVICE_REGISTRY_DESIGN.md`, `DOCKER_EVENT_LISTENER_DESIGN.md`.*","operationIsLocatedInWorkspace":true,"startLineNumbers":[]}

8. `GET /api/v1/events` — Stream SSE avec filtres (service, type, severity, since), pagination cursor
9. `WS /api/v1/ws/events` — WebSocket bidirectionnel avec subscribe/unsubscribe et ping/pong

Il répond à des questions critiques :\n\n```\n\"Si Kafka meurt, qu'est-ce qui est impacté ?\"\n\"Dans quel ordre dois-je démarrer les services ?\"\n\"Y a-t-il des cycles de dépendance dans le système ?\"\n\"Quel est le chemin critique du startup ?\"\n```\n\n---\n\n## 2. GRAPH DATA STRUCTURE\n\n### 2.1 Adjacency Representation\n\n```\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                    DIRECTED GRAPH (DAG)                          │\n│                                                                  │\n│  Nodes: Services (service_id, group, role, health)              │\n│  Edges: Dependencies (dependent → dependency, weight, type)      │\n│                                                                  │\n│  Convention:                                                     │\n│    Edge A ──► B  means \"A depends on B\"                          │\n│    (B must be running before A can start)                        │\n│                                                                  │\n│  Example:                                                        │\n│                                                                  │\n│    osiris-worker-ai ──► osiris-infra-kafka                       │\n│    osiris-worker-ai ──► osiris-worker-graph ──► osiris-data-memgraph                  │\n│    osiris-gateway-api ──► osiris-data-postgres                   │\n│    osiris-gateway-api ──► osiris-data-redis                      │\n│    osiris-gateway-api ──► osiris-data-memgraph                   │\n│    osiris-gateway-api ──► osiris-infra-kafka                     │\n│    osiris-gateway-cp ──► osiris-infra-kafka                      │\n│    osiris-obs-prometheus ──► osiris-infra-kafka                   │\n│    osiris-obs-grafana ──► osiris-obs-prometheus                   │\n│    osiris-obs-grafana ──► osiris-obs-loki                        │\n│    osiris-worker-threat ──► osiris-infra-kafka                    │\n│    osiris-worker-geoint ──► osiris-infra-kafka                    │\n│    osiris-worker-digitaltwin ──► osiris-infra-kafka               │\n│    osiris-worker-predictive ──► osiris-infra-kafka                │\n│    osiris-worker-policy ──► osiris-infra-kafka                    │\n│    osiris-worker-reward ──► osiris-infra-kafka                    │\n│    osiris-worker-cp-engine ──► osiris-infra-kafka                 │\n│    osiris-worker-incident-replay ──► osiris-infra-kafka           │\n│    osiris-worker-selfhealing ──► osiris-infra-kafka               │\n│    osiris-worker-selfrewrite ──► osiris-infra-kafka               │\n│                                                                  │\n│  Visual:                                                         │\n│                                                                  │\n│         ┌─────────────────────┐                                  │\n│         │  osiris-infra-kafka │ ◄── Hub node (12 dependents)     │\n│         └──┬──┬──┬──┬──┬──┬──┘                                  │\n│            │  │  │  │  │  │                                      │\n│     ┌──────┘  │  │  │  │  └──────┐                              │\n│     ▼         ▼  │  ▼  │         ▼                              │\n│  ┌──────┐ ┌────┐ │┌────┐     ┌──────────┐                       │\n│  │worker│ │gate│ ││obs-│     │worker-   │                       │\n│  │  -ai │ │way │ ││prom│     │graph     │                       │\n│  └──┬───┘ └─┬──┘ │└────┘     └────┬─────┘                       │\n│     │       │    │                 │                             │\n│     ▼       ▼    │                 ▼                             │\n│  ┌──────┐ ┌────┐ │            ┌──────────┐                       │\n│  │ollama│ │pg  │ │            │memgraph  │                       │\n│  │qdrant│ │redis│            └──────────┘                       │\n│  └──────┘ └────┘                                                │\n│                                                                  │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\n### 2.2 Internal Data Model\n\n```python\nfrom __future__ import annotations\nfrom enum import Enum\nfrom typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Set, Tuple\nfrom pydantic import BaseModel, Field\nfrom datetime import datetime\nimport uuid\n\n\nclass DependencyType(str, Enum):\n    STARTUP   = \"startup\"    # Must be running before dependent can start\n    RUNTIME   = \"runtime\"    # Required during operation (soft dependency)\n    CONFIG    = \"config\"     # Depends on config being available\n    SCRAPE    = \"scrape\"     # Prometheus scrape target (observability dep)\n\n\nclass DependencyWeight(int, Enum):\n    \"\"\"Criticality weight — higher = more critical.\"\"\"\n    CRITICAL  = 10   # Dependent fails immediately if this is down\n    HIGH      = 7    # Dependent degrades significantly\n    MEDIUM    = 4    # Dependent partially functional\n    LOW       = 1    # Dependent mostly functional without this\n\n\nclass GraphNode(BaseModel):\n    \"\"\"A service node in the dependency graph.\"\"\"\n    service_id: str\n    group: str\n    role: str\n    lifecycle: str           # Current lifecycle state\n    health: str              # Current health state\n    health_score: int        # 0-100\n    is_running: bool         # Convenience flag\n    in_degree: int = 0       # Number of incoming edges (how many depend on this)\n    out_degree: int = 0      # Number of outgoing edges (how many this depends on)\n    metadata: Dict[str, Any] = {}\n\n\nclass GraphEdge(BaseModel):\n    \"\"\"A dependency edge in the graph.\"\"\"\n    edge_id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4())[:8])\n    dependent: str           # Service that depends on another (A in A→B)\n    dependency: str          # Service being depended on (B in A→B)\n    weight: DependencyWeight = DependencyWeight.HIGH\n    dep_type: DependencyType = DependencyType.RUNTIME\n    is_required: bool = True\n    timeout_seconds: int = 300\n    metadata: Dict[str, Any] = {}\n\n\nclass GraphSnapshot(BaseModel):\n    \"\"\"Immutable snapshot of the dependency graph at a point in time.\"\"\"\n    snapshot_id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))\n    timestamp: datetime = Field(default_factory=datetime.utcnow)\n    nodes: Dict[str, GraphNode]\n    edges: List[GraphEdge]\n    adjacency: Dict[str, List[str]]     # service → [dependencies]\n    reverse_adj: Dict[str, List[str]]   # service → [dependents]\n    metadata: Dict[str, Any] = {}\n\n\nclass TopologicalOrder(BaseModel):\n    \"\"\"Result of topological sort.\"\"\"\n    layers: List[List[str]]              # Each layer can start in parallel\n    total_services: int\n    critical_path: List[str]             # Longest chain\n    critical_path_length: int\n    has_cycles: bool\n    cycles: List[List[str]]              # List of circular dependency chains\n```\n\n---\n\n## 3. ALGORITHMS\n\n### 3.1 Topological Sort (Kahn's Algorithm)\n\n**Purpose** : Determine the correct startup order.\n\n```\nAlgorithm: Kahn's Algorithm (BFS-based Topological Sort)\n\nInput:  Directed graph G = (V, E) where edge A→B means \"A depends on B\"\nOutput: Layered topological order + cycle detection\n\nPROCEDURE topological_sort(G):\n    in_degree = {v: 0 for v in G.nodes}\n    for each edge (A → B) in G.edges:\n        in_degree[A] += 1\n    \n    # Layer 0: nodes with no dependencies\n    layers = []\n    current_layer = [v for v in G.nodes if in_degree[v] == 0]\n    \n    while current_layer is not empty:\n        layers.append(current_layer)\n        next_layer = []\n        for v in current_layer:\n            for each dependent u of v:  # edges v → u means u depends on v\n                in_degree[u] -= 1\n                if in_degree[u] == 0:\n                    next_layer.append(u)\n        current_layer = next_layer\n    \n    # Cycle detection\n    if sum(in_degree.values()) > 0:\n        cycles = find_cycles(G, in_degree)\n        return layers, cycles\n    \n    return layers, []\n\nTime Complexity:  O(V + E)\nSpace Complexity: O(V)\n```\n\n**Application in Osiris :**\n\n```\nLayer 0 (bootstrap — no deps):     [osiris-infra-kafka]\nLayer 1 (depends only on Kafka):   [schema-registry, all workers, gateway-api, gateway-cp]\nLayer 2 (depends on Layer 1):      [obs-prometheus, obs-loki]\nLayer 3 (depends on Layer 2):      [obs-grafana]\n```\n\n### 3.2 Circular Dependency Detection (DFS)\n\n**Purpose** : Find and report cycles that would deadlock startup.\n\n```\nAlgorithm: DFS with Back-Edge Detection\n\nPROCEDURE find_cycles(G):\n    visited = {}     # WHITE=unvisited, GRAY=in-progress, BLACK=done\n    parent = {}\n    cycles = []\n    \n    for v in G.nodes:\n        visited[v] = WHITE\n    \n    for v in G.nodes:\n        if visited[v] == WHITE:\n            path = dfs_visit(G, v, visited, parent, [])\n            if path:\n                cycles.append(path)\n    \n    return cycles\n\nPROCEDURE dfs_visit(G, u, visited, parent, path):\n    visited[u] = GRAY\n    path.append(u)\n    \n    for v in G.adjacency[u]:  # u depends on v\n        if visited[v] == GRAY:\n            # Back edge found → cycle!\n            cycle_start = path.index(v)\n            return path[cycle_start:] + [v]\n        elif visited[v] == WHITE:\n            result = dfs_visit(G, v, visited, parent, path)\n            if result:\n                return result\n    \n    visited[u] = BLACK\n    path.pop()\n    return None\n\nTime Complexity:  O(V + E)\nSpace Complexity: O(V)\n```\n\n**Example detection :**\n```\nIf somehow: A → B → C → A\n\nDetection output:\n  cycle: [A, B, C, A]\n  severity: critical\n  recommendation: \"Break cycle by making C→A optional (is_required=false)\"\n```\n\n### 3.3 Critical Path Analysis\n\n**Purpose** : Find the longest dependency chain (determines minimum startup time).\n\n```\nAlgorithm: Longest Path in DAG (via DP on topological order)\n\nPROCEDURE critical_path(G, topo_order):\n    # dist[v] = length of longest path from any root to v\n    dist = {v: 0 for v in G.nodes}\n    prev = {v: None for v in G.nodes}\n    \n    for layer in topo_order.layers:\n        for v in layer:\n            for dependent u of v:  # edge v→u means u depends on v\n                new_dist = dist[v] + weight(v→u)\n                if new_dist > dist[u]:\n                    dist[u] = new_dist\n                    prev[u] = v\n    \n    # Find node with maximum distance (end of critical path)\n    end_node = max(dist, key=dist.get)\n    \n    # Trace back\n    path = []\n    current = end_node\n    while current is not None:\n        path.append(current)\n        current = prev[current]\n    path.reverse()\n    \n    return path, dist[end_node]\n```\n\n**Osiris critical path :**\n```\nosiris-infra-kafka → osiris-data-postgres → osiris-gateway-api → osiris-obs-grafana\n   (0s)                (+5s)                 (+10s)              (+15s)\n                                                            Total: ~30s\n```\n\n### 3.4 Blast Radius Analysis\n\n**Purpose** : When a service fails, which services are impacted?\n\n```\nAlgorithm: BFS/DFS from failure node through reverse edges\n\nPROCEDURE blast_radius(G, failed_service, max_depth=10):\n    impacted = []\n    visited = set()\n    queue = [(failed_service, 0)]  # (service, depth)\n    \n    while queue:\n        current, depth = queue.pop(0)\n        if current in visited or depth > max_depth:\n            continue\n        visited.add(current)\n        \n        # Find all services that depend on 'current'\n        dependents = G.reverse_adj.get(current, [])\n        \n        for dep in dependents:\n            if dep not in visited:\n                impacted.append({\n                    \"service\": dep,\n                    \"depth\": depth + 1,\n                    \"weight\": get_edge_weight(dep, current),\n                    \"type\": get_edge_type(dep, current),\n                })\n                queue.append((dep, depth + 1))\n    \n    return impacted\n\nTime Complexity:  O(V + E) — BFS\nSpace Complexity: O(V)\n```\n\n**Example — Kafka failure blast radius :**\n```\nImpact on osiris-infra-kafka failure:\n\nDepth 1 (direct dependents — CRITICAL):\n  ├── osiris-gateway-api        (weight: CRITICAL, type: runtime)\n  ├── osiris-gateway-cp         (weight: CRITICAL, type: runtime)\n  ├── osiris-worker-ai          (weight: CRITICAL, type: runtime)\n  ├── osiris-worker-graph       (weight: CRITICAL, type: runtime)\n  ├── osiris-worker-threat      (weight: HIGH, type: runtime)\n  ├── osiris-worker-geoint      (weight: HIGH, type: runtime)\n  ├── osiris-worker-digitaltwin (weight: HIGH, type: runtime)\n  ├── osiris-worker-predictive  (weight: HIGH, type: runtime)\n  ├── osiris-worker-policy      (weight: HIGH, type: runtime)\n  ├── osiris-worker-reward      (weight: HIGH, type: runtime)\n  ├── osiris-worker-cp-engine   (weight: HIGH, type: runtime)\n  ├── osiris-worker-incident-replay (weight: HIGH, type: runtime)\n  ├── osiris-worker-selfhealing (weight: HIGH, type: runtime)\n  ├── osiris-worker-selfrewrite (weight: HIGH, type: runtime)\n  └── osiris-obs-prometheus     (weight: MEDIUM, type: scrape)\n\nDepth 2 (indirect — through gateway-api):\n  └── osiris-obs-grafana        (weight: MEDIUM, type: runtime)\n\nTotal impacted: 16 services (64% of platform)\n```\n\n### 3.5 Dependency Impact Score\n\n```\nPROCEDURE impact_score(G, failed_service):\n    \"\"\"Compute a 0-100 impact score for a service failure.\"\"\"\n    \n    direct = G.reverse_adj.get(failed_service, [])\n    \n    # Factor 1: Number of direct dependents (normalized)\n    count_score = min(len(direct) / 10, 1.0) * 30  # Max 30 points\n    \n    # Factor 2: Weight of most critical dependent\n    max_weight = max([e.weight for e in G.edges if e.dependency == failed_service], default=0)\n    weight_score = (max_weight / 10) * 30  # Max 30 points\n    \n    # Factor 3: Total downstream impact (BFS depth)\n    impacted = blast_radius(G, failed_service)\n    downstream_score = min(len(impacted) / 20, 1.0) * 25  # Max 25 points\n    \n    # Factor 4: Is it a hub node? (in_degree > threshold)\n    hub_score = (1.0 if len(direct) > 5 else len(direct) / 5) * 15  # Max 15 points\n    \n    total = int(count_score + weight_score + downstream_score + hub_score)\n    return min(max(total, 0), 100)\n```\n\n**Impact scores for key services :**\n```\nosiris-infra-kafka:          95/100 (hub node — 12 direct dependents)\nosiris-data-postgres:        45/100 (2 direct dependents, critical)\nosiris-data-memgraph:        40/100 (2 direct dependents)\nosiris-data-redis:           35/100 (1 direct dependent, critical)\nosiris-worker-ai:            15/100 (0 direct dependents, leaf)\nosiris-obs-grafana:           5/100 (0 direct dependents, leaf)\n```\n\n---\n\n## 4. GRAPH ENGINE IMPLEMENTATION\n\n```python\nclass DependencyGraphEngine:\n    \"\"\"\n    Core dependency graph engine.\n    Builds, analyzes, and serves the service dependency graph.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, registry: ServiceRegistry, config: PlatformConfig):\n        self._registry = registry\n        self._config = config\n        self._snapshot: Optional[GraphSnapshot] = None\n        self._lock = asyncio.Lock()\n\n    async def build_graph(self) -> GraphSnapshot:\n        \"\"\"Build graph from registry + config sources.\"\"\"\n        \n        async with self._lock:\n            nodes = {}\n            edges = []\n            \n            # Source 1: Services from registry\n            services = await self._registry.get_all_active()\n            for svc in services:\n                nodes[svc.service_id] = GraphNode(\n                    service_id=svc.service_id,\n                    group=svc.group_name,\n                    role=svc.role,\n                    lifecycle=svc.lifecycle_state,\n                    health=svc.health_state,\n                    health_score=svc.health_score.total,\n                    is_running=(svc.lifecycle_state == \"running\"),\n                )\n            \n            # Source 2: Dependencies from config (platform.yaml)\n            config_deps = self._config.get_dependencies()\n            \n            # Source 3: Dependencies from Docker labels\n            docker_deps = self._extract_docker_dependencies(services)\n            \n            # Merge (config takes precedence over Docker labels)\n            all_deps = {**docker_deps, **self._parse_config_deps(config_deps)}\n            \n            for dep in all_deps.values():\n                edges.append(dep)\n            \n            # Build adjacency lists\n            adjacency = self._build_adjacency(nodes, edges)\n            reverse_adj = self._build_reverse_adjacency(nodes, edges)\n            \n            # Update degrees\n            for node_id, node in nodes.items():\n                node.in_degree = len(reverse_adj.get(node_id, []))\n                node.out_degree = len(adjacency.get(node_id, []))\n            \n            self._snapshot = GraphSnapshot(\n                nodes=nodes,\n                edges=edges,\n                adjacency=adjacency,\n                reverse_adj=reverse_adj,\n            )\n            \n            return self._snapshot\n\n    def get_snapshot(self) -> Optional[GraphSnapshot]:\n        return self._snapshot\n\n    async def get_startup_order(self) -> TopologicalOrder:\n        \"\"\"Compute startup order using Kahn's algorithm.\"\"\"\n        \n        snapshot = self._snapshot or await self.build_graph()\n        \n        # Kahn's algorithm\n        in_degree = {nid: 0 for nid in snapshot.nodes}\n        for edge in snapshot.edges:\n            in_degree[edge.dependent] += 1\n        \n        layers = []\n        current = [nid for nid, deg in in_degree.items() if deg == 0]\n        \n        while current:\n            layers.append(sorted(current))  # Sort for deterministic order\n            next_layer = []\n            for nid in current:\n                for dep in snapshot.reverse_adj.get(nid, []):\n                    in_degree[dep] -= 1\n                    if in_degree[dep] == 0:\n                        next_layer.append(dep)\n            current = next_layer\n        \n        # Check for cycles\n        has_cycles = any(deg > 0 for deg in in_degree.values())\n        cycles = []\n        if has_cycles:\n            cycles = self._find_cycles(snapshot)\n        \n        # Critical path\n        crit_path, crit_len = self._compute_critical_path(snapshot, layers)\n        \n        return TopologicalOrder(\n            layers=layers,\n            total_services=len(snapshot.nodes),\n            critical_path=crit_path,\n            critical_path_length=crit_len,\n            has_cycles=has_cycles,\n            cycles=cycles,\n        )\n\n    def get_blast_radius(self, service_id: str, max_depth: int = 10) -> List[dict]:\n        \"\"\"Compute blast radius of a service failure.\"\"\"\n        \n        snapshot = self._snapshot\n        if not snapshot:\n            return []\n        \n        impacted = []\n        visited = set()\n        queue = [(service_id, 0)]\n        \n        while queue:\n            current, depth = queue.pop(0)\n            if current in visited or depth > max_depth:\n                continue\n            visited.add(current)\n            \n            dependents = snapshot.reverse_adj.get(current, [])\n            for dep_id in dependents:\n                if dep_id not in visited:\n                    edge = self._find_edge(snapshot.edges, dep_id, current)\n                    impacted.append({\n                        \"service\": dep_id,\n                        \"depth\": depth + 1,\n                        \"weight\": edge.weight.value if edge else 5,\n                        \"weight_label\": edge.weight.name if edge else \"MEDIUM\",\n                        \"type\": edge.dep_type.value if edge else \"runtime\",\n                        \"group\": snapshot.nodes[dep_id].group if dep_id in snapshot.nodes else \"unknown\",\n                    })\n                    queue.append((dep_id, depth + 1))\n        \n        return sorted(impacted, key=lambda x: (x[\"depth\"], -x[\"weight\"]))\n\n    def get_impact_score(self, service_id: str) -> dict:\n        \"\"\"Compute 0-100 impact score for a service failure.\"\"\"\n        \n        snapshot = self._snapshot\n        if not snapshot or service_id not in snapshot.nodes:\n            return {\"score\": 0, \"level\": \"none\"}\n        \n        direct = snapshot.reverse_adj.get(service_id, [])\n        \n        count_score = min(len(direct) / 10, 1.0) * 30\n        \n        max_weight = 0\n        for edge in snapshot.edges:\n            if edge.dependency == service_id:\n                max_weight = max(max_weight, edge.weight.value)\n        weight_score = (max_weight / 10) * 30\n        \n        impacted = self.get_blast_radius(service_id)\n        downstream_score = min(len(impacted) / 20, 1.0) * 25\n        \n        hub_score = (1.0 if len(direct) > 5 else len(direct) / 5) * 15\n        \n        total = int(count_score + weight_score + downstream_score + hub_score)\n        total = min(max(total, 0), 100)\n        \n        level = \"critical\" if total >= 70 else \"high\" if total >= 40 else \"medium\" if total >= 20 else \"low\"\n        \n        return {\n            \"score\": total,\n            \"level\": level,\n            \"breakdown\": {\n                \"direct_dependents\": len(direct),\n                \"max_weight\": max_weight,\n                \"total_downstream\": len(impacted),\n                \"is_hub_node\": len(direct) > 5,\n            }\n        }\n\n    def _find_cycles(self, snapshot: GraphSnapshot) -> List[List[str]]:\n        \"\"\"Find all cycles using DFS.\"\"\"\n        WHITE, GRAY, BLACK = 0, 1, 2\n        color = {nid: WHITE for nid in snapshot.nodes}\n        cycles = []\n        \n        def dfs(u, path):\n            color[u] = GRAY\n            path.append(u)\n            for v in snapshot.adjacency.get(u, []):\n                if color[v] == GRAY:\n                    idx = path.index(v)\n                    cycles.append(path[idx:] + [v])\n                elif color[v] == WHITE:\n                    dfs(v, path)\n            color[u] = BLACK\n            path.pop()\n        \n        for nid in snapshot.nodes:\n            if color[nid] == WHITE:\n                dfs(nid, [])\n        \n        return cycles\n\n    def _compute_critical_path(\n        self, snapshot: GraphSnapshot, layers: List[List[str]]\n    ) -> Tuple[List[str], int]:\n        \"\"\"Find the longest dependency chain.\"\"\"\n        dist = {nid: 0 for nid in snapshot.nodes}\n        prev = {nid: None for nid in snapshot.nodes}\n        \n        for layer in layers:\n            for nid in layer:\n                for dep_id in snapshot.reverse_adj.get(nid, []):\n                    edge = self._find_edge(snapshot.edges, dep_id, nid)\n                    w = edge.weight.value if edge else 1\n                    if dist[nid] + w > dist[dep_id]:\n                        dist[dep_id] = dist[nid] + w\n                        prev[dep_id] = nid\n        \n        end_node = max(dist, key=dist.get)\n        path = []\n        current = end_node\n        while current is not None:\n            path.append(current)\n            current = prev[current]\n        path.reverse()\n        \n        return path, dist[end_node]\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def _find_edge(edges, dependent, dependency):\n        for e in edges:\n            if e.dependent == dependent and e.dependency == dependency:\n                return e\n        return None\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def _build_adjacency(nodes, edges):\n        adj = {nid: [] for nid in nodes}\n        for edge in edges:\n            adj[edge.dependent].append(edge.dependency)\n        return adj\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def _build_reverse_adjacency(nodes, edges):\n        rev = {nid: [] for nid in nodes}\n        for edge in edges:\n            rev[edge.dependency].append(edge.dependent)\n        return rev\n```\n\n---\n\n## 5. ### Tour 1971 — Assistant

*2026-06-16 13:06:32 UTC*

Moteur de graphe de dépendances conçu et documenté dans `DEPENDENCY_GRAPH_ENGINE.md`.

**Data Structure (5 modèles Pydantic) :**
- `GraphNode` — service_id, group, role, lifecycle, health, health_score, in_degree, out_degree
- `GraphEdge` — dependent, dependency, weight (CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW), dep_type (startup/runtime/config/scrape), is_required
- `GraphSnapshot` — immutable snapshot avec adjacency + reverse_adj lists
- `TopologicalOrder` — layers, critical_path, cycles détectés
- `DependencyType` et `DependencyWeight` — enums avec 4 types et 4 niveaux de criticité

**5 Algorithmes (tous O(V+E), < 1ms pour 25 services) :**
1. **Topological Sort** (Kahn's BFS) — startup order en couches parallèles
2. **Cycle Detection** (DFS with back-edge) — WHITE/GRAY/BLACK coloration
3. **Critical Path Analysis** (DP on topo order) — plus longue chaîne de dépendances
4. **Blast Radius** (BFS on reverse edges) — impact en cascade avec profondeur et poids
5. **Impact Score** (composite 0-100) — 4 facteurs : count, weight, downstream, hub

**6 API Endpoints :**
- `GET /api/v1/graph` — DAG complet en couches
- `GET /api/v1/graph/blast/{service_id}` — blast radius + impact score
- `GET /api/v1/graph/startup-order` — ordre de démarrage avec estimations temps
- `GET /api/v1/graph/cycles` — détection de cycles circulaires
- `GET /api/v1/graph/node/{service_id}` — détail d'un nœud
- `GET /api/v1/graph/mermaid` — diagramme Mermaid text/plain

**Exemple concret Osiris :**
- Kafka est le hub node critique (95/100, 12 dependents directs, 64% de la plateforme impactée)
- 5 couches de startup, temps total estimé ~45s
- Chemin critique : kafka → postgres → gateway → grafanaHAS_CHANGES

SCORING FORMULA\n\n### 3.1 Service Health Score (0–100)\n\n```python\nclass HealthScoringEngine:\n    \"\"\"\n    Computes health score 0-100 for each service.\n    \n    Score = Σ(weight_i × signal_i) × confidence_modifier × trend_modifier\n    \n    Where:\n        weight_i  = importance weight of signal i\n        signal_i  = normalized signal value (0-100)\n        confidence_modifier = based on data completeness\n        trend_modifier = based on score trajectory\n    \"\"\"\n    \n    # ── Signal Weights (must sum to 1.0) ──────────────────────\n    \n    SIGNAL_WEIGHTS = {\n        \"lifecycle\":      0.10,   # Is the container running?\n        \"http_health\":    0.25,   # Does /health endpoint respond?\n        \"tcp_health\":     0.10,   # Is the port reachable?\n        \"dependency\":     0.20,   # Are dependencies healthy?\n        \"uptime\":         0.15,   # How stable is it over time?\n        \"latency\":        0.10,   # Response time of health endpoint\n        \"error_rate\":     0.10,   # Health check failure rate\n    }\n    \n    # ── Individual Signal Scoring ─────────────────────────────\n    \n    def score_lifecycle(self, state: str) -> float:\n        \"\"\"0-100 based on container lifecycle state.\"\"\"\n        return {\n            \"running\":  100,\n            \"starting\": 50,\n            \"stopped\":  0,\n            \"dead\":     0,\n            \"pending\":  25,\n            \"unknown\":  10,\n        }.get(state, 10)\n    \n    def score_http_health(self, result: str, latency_ms: float) -> float:\n        \"\"\"0-100 based on HTTP health check result.\"\"\"\n        if result == \"pass\":\n            # Bonus for fast response\n            if latency_ms < 100:\n                return 100\n            elif latency_ms < 500:\n                return 90\n            elif latency_ms < 2000:\n                return 75\n            else:\n                return 60  # Slow but alive\n        elif result == \"timeout\":\n            return 20\n        elif result == \"error\":\n            return 0\n        else:\n            return 50  # Unknown = uncertain\n    \n    def score_tcp_health(self, result: str) -> float:\n        \"\"\"0-100 based on TCP connectivity check.\"\"\"\n        return {\n            \"pass\":    100,\n            \"timeout\": 20,\n            \"fail\":    0,\n            \"error\":   0,\n        }.get(result, 50)\n    \n    def score_dependency(self, dep_scores: List[float], \n                          weights: List[float]) -> float:\n        \"\"\"\n        Weighted average of dependency health scores.\n        Required deps weighted 3x more than optional deps.\n        \"\"\"\n        if not dep_scores:\n            return 100  # No deps = perfect score\n        \n        weighted_sum = sum(s * w for s, w in zip(dep_scores, weights))\n        total_weight = sum(weights) if weights else 1\n        return weighted_sum / total_weight\n    \n    def score_uptime(self, restart_count: int, \n                      consecutive_failures: int,\n                      uptime_seconds: float) -> float:\n        \"\"\"\n        0-100 based on operational stability.\n        \n        Factors:\n        - Recent restarts (last 1h) penalize heavily\n        - Consecutive failures penalize exponentially\n        - Long uptime with no restarts = bonus\n        \"\"\"\n        score = 100.0\n        \n        # Penalty for restarts (last 1h window)\n        recent_restarts = self._count_recent_restarts(restart_count, uptime_seconds)\n        score -= min(recent_restarts * 15, 60)  # Max -60%\n        \n        # Penalty for consecutive failures (exponential)\n        score -= min(consecutive_failures ** 2 * 10, 40)  # Max -40%\n        \n        # Bonus for uptime > 1 hour with no restarts\n        if uptime_seconds > 3600 and recent_restarts == 0:\n            score = min(score + 5, 100)\n        \n        # Bonus for uptime > 24h with no restarts\n        if uptime_seconds > 86400 and recent_restarts == 0:\n            score = min(score + 10, 100)\n        \n        return max(score, 0)\n    \n    def score_latency(self, latency_ms: float, \n                       p99_ms: float) -> float:\n        \"\"\"\n        0-100 based on response latency.\n        \n        Uses percentile-based scoring against historical baseline.\n        \"\"\"\n        if latency_ms is None:\n            return 50  # No data = uncertain\n        \n        if p99_ms is None or p99_ms == 0:\n            p99_ms = 1000  # Default baseline\n        \n        ratio = latency_ms / p99_ms\n        \n        if ratio < 0.5:\n            return 100  # Well below baseline\n        elif ratio < 1.0:\n            return 90   # Within normal range\n        elif ratio < 1.5:\n            return 70   # Slightly elevated\n        elif ratio < 3.0:\n            return 40   # Significantly elevated\n        elif ratio < 10.0:\n            return 15   # Severe degradation\n        else:\n            return 0    # Effectively unresponsive\n    \n    def score_error_rate(self, failures: int, total: int) -> float:\n        \"\"\"\n        0-100 based on health check failure rate.\n        \"\"\"\n        if total == 0:\n            return 50  # No checks = uncertain\n        \n        rate = failures / total\n        \n        if rate == 0:\n            return 100\n        elif rate < 0.01:\n            return 95   # <1% failures\n        elif rate < 0.05:\n            return 85   # <5% failures\n        elif rate < 0.10:\n            return 70   # <10% failures\n        elif rate < 0.25:\n            return 40   # <25% failures\n        elif rate < 0.50:\n            return 15   # <50% failures\n        else:\n            return 0    # >50% failures\n    \n    # ── Composite Score ───────────────────────────────────────\n    \n    def compute_service_score(\n        self,\n        lifecycle_state: str,\n        http_result: str,\n        http_latency_ms: float,\n        tcp_result: str,\n        dep_scores: List[float],\n        dep_weights: List[float],\n        restart_count: int,\n        consecutive_failures: int,\n        uptime_seconds: float,\n        p99_latency_ms: float,\n        recent_failures: int,\n        recent_checks: int,\n    ) -> ServiceHealthScore:\n        \n        # Compute individual signals\n        signals = {\n            \"lifecycle\":   self.score_lifecycle(lifecycle_state),\n            \"http_health\": self.score_http_health(http_result, http_latency_ms),\n            \"tcp_health\":  self.score_tcp_health(tcp_result),\n            \"dependency\":  self.score_dependency(dep_scores, dep_weights),\n            \"uptime\":      self.score_uptime(restart_count, consecutive_failures, uptime_seconds),\n            \"latency\":     self.score_latency(http_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms),\n            \"error_rate\":  self.score_error_rate(recent_failures, recent_checks),\n        }\n        \n        # Weighted sum\n        raw_score = sum(\n            signals[signal] * weight \n            for signal, weight in self.SIGNAL_WEIGHTS.items()\n        )\n        \n        # Confidence modifier (based on data completeness)\n        available_signals = sum(1 for s in signals.values() if s is not None)\n        confidence = available_signals / len(self.SIGNAL_WEIGHTS)\n        confidence_modifier = 0.7 + (0.3 * confidence)  # Range: 0.7 to 1.0\n        \n        # Apply modifier\n        adjusted_score = raw_score * confidence_modifier\n        \n        # Clamp to 0-100\n        final_score = int(min(max(adjusted_score, 0), 100))\n        \n        # Determine status from score\n        status = self._score_to_status(final_score)\n        \n        return ServiceHealthScore(\n            score=final_score,\n            status=status,\n            signals=signals,\n            confidence=round(confidence, 2),\n            confidence_modifier=round(confidence_modifier, 2),\n            raw_score=round(raw_score, 1),\n        )\n    \n    @staticmethod\n    def _score_to_status(score: int) -> str:\n        if score >= 80:\n            return \"healthy\"\n        elif score >= 50:\n            return \"degraded\"\n        elif score >= 20:\n            return \"unhealthy\"\n        else:\n            return \"critical\"\n\n\nclass ServiceHealthScore(BaseModel):\n    \"\"\"Complete health score with breakdown.\"\"\"\n    score: int                          # 0-100\n    status: str                         # healthy|degraded|unhealthy|critical\n    signals: Dict[str, float]           # Per-signal scores\n    confidence: float                   # 0-1 (data completeness)\n    confidence_modifier: float          # Applied modifier\n    raw_score: float                    # Before modifier\n```\n\n### 3.2 Score-to-Status Mapping\n\n```\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  SCORE → STATUS MAPPING                                         │\n│                                                                  │\n│  100 ┤ ████████████████████████████████████████ HEALTHY          │\n│   80 ┤ ████████████████████████████████████████ (≥80)            │\n│      │                                                           │\n│   79 ┤ ▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓ DEGRADED       │\n│   50 ┤ ▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓ (50-79)         │\n│      │                                                           │\n│   49 ┤ ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ UNHEALTHY      │\n│   20 ┤ ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ (20-49)         │\n│      │                                                           │\n│   19 ┤ ▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒ CRITICAL       │\n│    0 ┤ ▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒ (0-19)          │\n│      └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────     │\n│                                                                  │\n│  Action triggers:                                                │\n│  ├── healthy    → no action                                     │\n│  ├── degraded   → log warning, reduce monitoring interval       │\n│  ├── unhealthy  → auto-restart (if configured), alert           │\n│  └── critical   → emergency alert, cascade check                │\n│                                                                  │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\n---\n\n## 4. PLATFORM-WIDE HEALTH AGGREGATION\n\n### 4.1 Platform Health Score\n\n```python\nclass PlatformHealthAggregator:\n    \"\"\"\n    Aggregates individual service scores into platform-wide metrics.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def compute_platform_score(\n        self, \n        service_scores: Dict[str, ServiceHealthScore],\n        services: Dict[str, ServiceRecord],\n    ) -> PlatformHealth:\n        \n        if not service_scores:\n            return PlatformHealth(score=0, status=\"unknown\")\n        \n        # ── Weighted average (by group criticality) ───────────\n        \n        GROUP_WEIGHTS = {\n            \"data\":    0.30,   # Data layer is most critical\n            \"infra\":   0.25,   # Kafka/Schema Registry\n            \"gateway\": 0.25,   # API layer\n            \"worker\":  0.10,   # Workers are stateless, can restart\n            \"ai\":      0.05,   # Ollama is optional\n            \"obs\":     0.05,   # Observability is nice-to-have\n        }\n        \n        group_scores = {}\n        group_counts = {}\n        \n        for svc_id, score in service_scores.items():\n            svc = services.get(svc_id)\n            if not svc:\n                continue\n            group = svc.group_name\n            group_scores.setdefault(group, []).append(score.score)\n            group_counts[group] = group_counts.get(group, 0) + 1\n        \n        # Compute group averages\n        group_avgs = {}\n        for group, scores in group_scores.items():\n            group_avgs[group] = sum(scores) / len(scores)\n        \n        # Compute weighted platform score\n        platform_score = 0\n        total_weight = 0\n        for group, weight in GROUP_WEIGHTS.items():\n            if group in group_avgs:\n                platform_score += group_avgs[group] * weight\n                total_weight += weight\n        \n        if total_weight > 0:\n            platform_score = int(platform_score / total_weight)\n        \n        # ── SLI/SLO computation ───────────────────────────────\n        \n        total = len(service_scores)\n        healthy = sum(1 for s in service_scores.values() if s.status == \"healthy\")\n        degraded = sum(1 for s in service_scores.values() if s.status == \"degraded\")\n        unhealthy = sum(1 for s in service_scores.values() if s.status == \"unhealthy\")\n        critical = sum(1 for s in service_scores.values() if s.status == \"critical\")\n        \n        availability_sli = (healthy + degraded * 0.5) / total if total > 0 else 0\n        error_budget_remaining = max(0, 1.0 - (1.0 - availability_sli) / 0.001)  # 99.9% SLO\n        \n        return PlatformHealth(\n            score=platform_score,\n            status=self._platform_status(platform_score, critical),\n            total_services=total,\n            healthy=healthy,\n            degraded=degraded,\n            unhealthy=unhealthy,\n            critical=critical,\n            availability_sli=round(availability_sli, 4),\n            error_budget_remaining=round(error_budget_remaining, 2),\n            group_scores=group_avgs,\n            worst_services=self._get_worst(service_scores, n=5),\n            best_services=self._get_best(service_scores, n=3),\n        )\n    \n    @staticmethod\n    def _platform_status(score, critical_count):\n        if critical_count > 0:\n            return \"critical\"\n        elif score >= 80:\n            return \"healthy\"\n        elif score >= 50:\n            return \"degraded\"\n        else:\n            return \"unhealthy\"\n    \n    @staticmethod\n    def _get_worst(scores, n=5):\n        return [\n            {\"service\": k, \"score\": v.score, \"status\": v.status}\n            for k, v in sorted(scores.items(), key=lambda x: x[1].score)[:n]\n        ]\n    \n    @staticmethod\n    def _get_best(scores, n=3):\n        return [\n            {\"service\": k, \"score\": v.score, \"status\": v.status}\n            for k, v in sorted(scores.items(), key=lambda x: x[1].score, reverse=True)[:n]\n        ]\n\n\nclass PlatformHealth(BaseModel):\n    score: int\n    status: str\n    total_services: int\n    healthy: int\n    degraded: int\n    unhealthy: int\n    critical: int\n    availability_sli: float          # 0-1\n    error_budget_remaining: float    # 0-1 (percentage of error budget left)\n    group_scores: Dict[str, float]\n    worst_services: List[dict]\n    best_services: List[dict]\n```\n\n### 4.2 SLI/SLO Model\n\n```\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  SLI/SLO FRAMEWORK                                              │\n│                                                                  │\n│  SLI (Service Level Indicator):                                  │\n│    availability = (healthy services) / (total services)          │\n│                                                                  │\n│  SLO (Service Level Objective):                                  │\n│    target = 99.9% availability                                  │\n│    window = rolling 30 days                                     │\n│                                                                  │\n│  Error Budget:                                                   │\n│    budget = 1 - SLO = 0.1% = 0.001                              │\n│    consumed = (1 - availability_sli) / budget                    │\n│    remaining = max(0, 1 - consumed)                             │\n│                                                                  │\n│  Example:                                                        │\n│    22/25 healthy = 88% availability                              │\n│    consumed = (1 - 0.88) / 0.001 = 120                          │\n│    remaining = 0 (budget exhausted!)                             │\n│                                                                  │\n│  But with weighted scoring:                                      │\n│    22 healthy (score 95) + 2 degraded (score 60) + 1 unhealthy  │\n│    availability_sli = (22*1.0 + 2*0.5 + 1*0.0) / 25 = 0.92     │\n│    consumed = (1 - 0.92) / 0.001 = 80                           │\n│    remaining = 0 (still exhausted)                               │\n│                                                                  │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\n---\n\n## 5. ANOMALY DETECTION\n\n```python\nclass AnomalyDetector:\n    \"\"\"\n    Detects health anomalies using score history and patterns.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, history_size: int = 100, alert_threshold: float = 0.3):\n        self._history: Dict[str, deque] = defaultdict(lambda: deque(maxlen=history_size))\n        self._alert_threshold = alert_threshold  # 30% score drop triggers alert\n    \n    def record_score(self, service_id: str, score: int, timestamp: datetime):\n        \"\"\"Record a score data point.\"\"\"\n        self._history[service_id].append((timestamp, score))\n    \n    def detect_anomalies(self, service_id: str, current_score: int) -> List[Anomaly]:\n        \"\"\"Check for various anomaly patterns.\"\"\"\n        \n        history = list(self._history.get(service_id, []))\n        anomalies = []\n        \n        # 1. Sudden score drop\n        if len(history) >= 2:\n            prev_score = history[-2][1]\n            drop = (prev_score - current_score) / max(prev_score, 1)\n            if drop > self._alert_threshold:\n                anomalies.append(Anomaly(\n                    type=\"score_drop\",\n                    severity=\"warning\" if drop < 0.5 else \"critical\",\n                    detail=f\"Score dropped from {prev_score} to {current_score} \"\n                           f\"({drop:.0%} decrease)\",\n                ))\n        \n        # 2. Oscillation (flapping)\n        if len(history) >= 6:\n            recent = [s for _, s in history[-6:]]\n            oscillations = sum(\n                1 for i in range(1, len(recent)) \n                if abs(recent[i] - recent[i-1]) > 20\n            )\n            if oscillations >= 3:\n                anomalies.append(Anomaly(\n                    type=\"oscillation\",\n                    severity=\"warning\",\n                    detail=f\"Score oscillating: {recent} \"\n                           f\"({oscillations} swings in last 6 checks)\",\n                ))\n        \n        # 3. Consistently degrading\n        if len(history) >= 5:\n            recent = [s for _, s in history[-5:]]\n            if all(recent[i] < recent[i-1] for i in range(1, len(recent))):\n                total_drop = recent[0] - recent[-1]\n                anomalies.append(Anomaly(\n                    type=\"trend_degradation\",\n                    severity=\"warning\" if total_drop < 30 else \"critical\",\n                    detail=f\"Score declining for 5 consecutive checks: \"\n                           f\"{recent[0]} → {recent[-1]}\",\n                ))\n        \n        # 4. Stale (no score update)\n        if history:\n            last_update = history[-1][0]\n            age_seconds = (datetime.utcnow() - last_update).total_seconds()\n            if age_seconds > 300:  # 5 minutes\n                anomalies.append(Anomaly(\n                    type=\"stale\",\n                    severity=\"warning\",\n                    detail=f\"No score update for {int(age_seconds)}s\",\n                ))\n        \n        # 5. Score below critical threshold\n        if current_score < 20:\n            anomalies.append(Anomaly(\n                type=\"critical_score\",\n                severity=\"critical\",\n                detail=f\"Score {current_score} is below critical threshold (20)\",\n            ))\n        \n        return anomalies\n    \n    def detect_cascade_failure(\n        self, \n        all_scores: Dict[str, ServiceHealthScore],\n    ) -> Optional[CascadeAlert]:\n        \"\"\"\n        Detect if multiple services are failing simultaneously\n        (potential cascade failure).\n        \"\"\"\n        unhealthy_services = [\n            sid for sid, score in all_scores.items()\n            if score.status in (\"unhealthy\", \"critical\")\n        ]\n        \n        if len(unhealthy_services) >= 3:\n            return CascadeAlert(\n                severity=\"critical\",\n                affected_services=unhealthy_services,\n                count=len(unhealthy_services),\n                message=f\"Cascade failure detected: {len(unhealthy_services)} \"\n                        f\"services unhealthy simultaneously\",\n            )\n        \n        return None\n\n\nclass Anomaly(BaseModel):\n    type: str           # score_drop|oscillation|trend_degradation|stale|critical_score\n    severity: str       # warning|critical\n    detail: str\n    detected_at: datetime = Field(default_factory=datetime.utcnow)\n\n\nclass CascadeAlert(BaseModel):\n    severity: str\n    affected_services: List[str]\n    count: int\n    message: str\n```\n\n### 5.1 Anomaly Detection Patterns\n\n```\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  ANOMALY PATTERN       │ CONDITION              │ SEVERITY       │\n├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│                        │                        │                │\n│  SCORE DROP            │ Δ > 30% from previous  │ warning        │\n│  ████████░░            │ Δ > 50% from previous  │ critical       │\n│  ──────►░░░░           │                        │                │\n│                        │                        │                │\n│  OSCILLATION           │ >3 swings of >20pts    │ warning        │\n│  █░█░█░█░             │ in last 6 checks       │                │\n│                        │                        │                │\n│  TREND DEGRADATION     │ 5 consecutive drops    │ warning/crit   │\n│  ████████░░░░░░░░      │                        │                │\n│                        │                        │                │\n│  STALE                 │ No update > 5min       │ warning        │\n│  ───────────────      │                        │                │\n│                        │                        │                │\n│  CRITICAL SCORE        │ Score < 20             │ critical       │\n│  ▓▓▓▓░░░░░░░░░░       │                        │                │\n│                        │                        │                │\n│  CASCADE FAILURE       │ ≥3 services unhealthy  │ critical       │\n│  ██████ (multiple)     │ simultaneously         │                │\n│                        │                        │                │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\n---\n\n## 6. METRICS INGESTION MODEL\n\n### 6.1 Signal Sources\n\n```\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  SIGNAL              │ SOURCE                │ INTERVAL         │\n├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│  lifecycle           │ Docker event stream   │ Real-time        │\n│  http_health         │ Health probe (GET)    │ 15s (configurable)│\n│  tcp_health          │ Health probe (TCP)    │ 15s              │\n│  dependency          │ Graph engine + probe  │ 30s              │\n│  uptime              │ Registry state        │ Real-time        │\n│  latency             │ HTTP probe response   │ 15s              │\n│  error_rate          │ Health probe history  │ Computed/15s     │\n│  cpu_usage           │ Docker stats API      │ 30s (optional)   │\n│  memory_usage        │ Docker stats API      │ 30s (optional)   │\n│  restart_count       │ Registry state        │ Real-time        │\n│  oom_killed          │ Docker events         │ Real-time        │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\n### 6.2 Ingestion Pipeline\n\n```\n  ┌──────────────┐     ┌──────────────┐     ┌──────────────┐\n  │ Health Probe │────►│              │     │              │\n  │ (HTTP/TCP)   │     │              │     │              │\n  └──────────────┘     │              │     │              │\n                       │   Signal     │     │   Health     │\n  ┌──────────────┐     │   Buffer     │────►│   Scoring    │\n  │ Docker Event │────►│              │     │   Engine     │\n  │ Listener     │     │ (per-service │     │              │\n  └──────────────┘     │  ring buffer)│     │  Score = f() │\n                       │              │     │              │\n  ┌──────────────┐     │              │     └──────┬───────┘\n  │ Graph Engine │────►│              │            │\n  │ (dep health) │     │              │            │\n  └──────────────┘     └──────────────┘            │\n                                                   │\n                              ┌─────────────────────┘\n                              │\n                    ┌─────────▼──────────┐\n                    │   Service Health   │\n                    │   Score Storage    │\n                    │   (in-memory +     │\n                    │    DB history)     │\n                    └─────────┬──────────┘\n                              │\n              ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐\n              │               │               │\n              ▼               ▼               ▼\n    ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐\n    │ Anomaly      │ │ Platform     │ │ API Response │\n    │ Detector     │ │ Aggregator   │ │ (GET /health)│\n    └──────┬───────┘ └──────┬───────┘ └──────────────┘\n           │                │\n           ▼                ▼\n    ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐\n    │ Alerting     │ │ Prometheus   │\n    │ Engine       │ │ Export       │\n    └──────────────┘ └──────────────┘\n```\n\n### 6.3 Signal Buffer\n\n```python\nclass SignalBuffer:\n    \"\"\"\n    Per-service ring buffer of recent signals.\n    Used for rolling calculations (error rate, trend, etc.).\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, max_size: int = 100):\n        self._signals: Dict[str, deque] = defaultdict(\n            lambda: deque(maxlen=max_size)\n        )\n    \n    def record(self, service_id: str, signal: HealthSignal):\n        self._signals[service_id].append(signal)\n    \n    def get_recent(self, service_id: str, n: int = 10) -> List[HealthSignal]:\n        \"\"\"Get last N signals for a service.\"\"\"\n        return list(self._signals[service_id])[-n:]\n    \n    def get_error_rate(self, service_id: str, window: int = 20) -> Tuple[int, int]:\n        \"\"\"Get (failures, total) for last N checks.\"\"\"\n        recent = self.get_recent(service_id, window)\n        failures = sum(1 for s in recent if s.result == \"fail\")\n        return failures, len(recent)\n    \n    def get_avg_latency(self, service_id: str, window: int = 10) -> Optional[float]:\n        \"\"\"Get average latency for last N checks.\"\"\"\n        recent = self.get_recent(service_id, window)\n        latencies = [s.latency_ms for s in recent if s.latency_ms is not None]\n        return sum(latencies) / len(latencies) if latencies else None\n    \n    def get_p99_latency(self, service_id: str) -> Optional[float]:\n        \"\"\"Get 99th percentile latency from history.\"\"\"\n        all_latencies = [\n            s.latency_ms for s in self._signals[service_id]\n            if s.latency_ms is not None\n        ]\n        if not all_latencies:\n            return None\n        all_latencies.sort()\n        idx = int(len(all_latencies) * 0.99)\n        return all_latencies[min(idx, len(all_latencies) - 1)]\n\n\nclass HealthSignal(BaseModel):\n    \"\"\"A single health check signal.\"\"\"\n    service_id: str\n    check_type: str         # http|tcp|cmd|passive\n    result: str             # pass|fail|timeout|error\n    latency_ms: Optional[float] = None\n    status_code: Optional[int] = None\n    detail: Optional[str] = None\n    timestamp: datetime = Field(default_factory=datetime.utcnow)\n```\n\n---\n\n## 7. ALERTING LOGIC\n\n### 7.1 Alert Rules\n\n```python\nclass AlertEngine:\n    \"\"\"\n    Generates alerts based on health scores and anomalies.\n    Supports deduplication, grouping, and escalation.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    ALERT_RULES = [\n        # ── Per-Service Alerts ─────────────────────────────\n        AlertRule(\n            name=\"service_critical\",\n            condition=lambda s: s.score < 20,\n            severity=\"critical\",\n            message_template=\"{service} is CRITICAL (score={score})\",\n            cooldown_seconds=300,\n            auto_action=\"restart\",\n        ),\n        AlertRule(\n            name=\"service_unhealthy\",\n            condition=lambda s: s.score < 50 and s.score >= 20,\n            severity=\"warning\",\n            message_template=\"{service} is UNHEALTHY (score={score})\",\n            cooldown_seconds=600,\n            auto_action=None,\n        ),\n        AlertRule(\n            name=\"service_degraded\",\n            condition=lambda s: s.score < 80 and s.score >= 50,\n            severity=\"info\",\n            message_template=\"{service} is DEGRADED (score={score})\",\n            cooldown_seconds=3600,\n            auto_action=None,\n        ),\n        AlertRule(\n            name=\"service_restarting\",\n            condition=lambda s: s.restart_count > 3,\n            severity=\"warning\",\n            message_template=\"{service} has restarted {restart_count} times\",\n            cooldown_seconds=1800,\n            auto_action=None,\n        ),\n        \n        # ── Platform Alerts ────────────────────────────────\n        AlertRule(\n            name=\"platform_critical\",\n            condition=lambda p: p.status == \"critical\",\n            severity=\"critical\",\n            message_template=\"Platform CRITICAL: {critical} services in critical state\",\n            cooldown_seconds=300,\n            auto_action=None,\n        ),\n        AlertRule(\n            name=\"platform_degraded\",\n            condition=lambda p: p.status == \"degraded\",\n            severity=\"warning\",\n            message_template=\"Platform DEGRADED: avg score {score}\",\n            cooldown_seconds=600,\n            auto_action=None,\n        ),\n        AlertRule(\n            name=\"error_budget_exhausted\",\n            condition=lambda p: p.error_budget_remaining <= 0,\n            severity=\"critical\",\n            message_template=\"Error budget EXHAUSTED — no more deployment changes allowed\",\n            cooldown_seconds=3600,\n            auto_action=None,\n        ),\n        AlertRule(\n            name=\"error_budget_low\",\n            condition=lambda p: 0 < p.error_budget_remaining <= 0.2,\n            severity=\"warning\",\n            message_template=\"Error budget LOW: {error_budget_remaining:.0%} remaining\",\n            cooldown_seconds=3600,\n            auto_action=None,\n        ),\n        \n        # ── Cascade Alerts ─────────────────────────────────\n        AlertRule(\n            name=\"cascade_failure\",\n            condition=lambda c: c is not None,\n            severity=\"critical\",\n            message_template=\"CASCADE FAILURE: {count} services unhealthy simultaneously\",\n            cooldown_seconds=300,\n            auto_action=\"emergency_stop\",\n        ),\n    ]\n```\n\n### 7.2 Alert Lifecycle\n\n```\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  ALERT LIFECYCLE                                                 │\n│                                                                  │\n│  ┌──────────┐     ┌──────────┐     ┌──────────┐                │\n│  │ DETECTED │────►│ PENDING  │────►│ FIRING   │                │\n│  └──────────┘     └──────────┘     └────┬─────┘                │\n│                                          │                       │\n│                              ┌───────────┼───────────┐          │\n│                              │           │           │          │\n│                              ▼           ▼           ▼          │\n│                         ┌────────┐  ┌────────┐  ┌────────┐     │\n│                         │ ACK'd  │  │RESOLVED│  │EXPIRED │     │\n│                         └────────┘  └────────┘  └────────┘     │\n│                                                                  │\n│  States:                                                         │\n│  ├── DETECTED: Anomaly/rule matched                              │\n│  ├── PENDING:  Waiting for cooldown to expire                    │\n│  ├── FIRING:   Active alert — notifications sent                 │\n│  ├── ACK'd:    Operator acknowledged                             │\n│  ├── RESOLVED: Condition no longer met                           │\n│  └── EXPIRED:  Alert auto-expired after TTL                      │\n│                                                                  │\n│  Deduplication:                                                  │\n│  ├── Same rule + same service = deduplicated (cooldown)          │\n│  ├── Different rules = separate alerts                           │\n│  └── Different services = separate alerts                        │\n│                                                                  │\n│  Escalation:                                                     │\n│  ├── warning (5min) → if unresolved → critical                   │\n│  ├── critical (15min) → if unresolved → page                     │\n│  └── page (30min) → if unresolved → escalate to lead             │\n│                                                                  │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\n### 7.3 Notification Channels\n\n```python\nclass NotificationChannel(BaseModel):\n    \"\"\"Defines a notification delivery channel.\"\"\"\n    name: str\n    type: str           # kafka|webhook|log|future_pagerduty\n    enabled: bool = True\n    severity_filter: List[str] = [\"warning\", \"critical\"]\n    \n    # Kafka channel (current)\n    kafka_topic: Optional[str] = \"osiris.alerts.critical\"\n    \n    # Webhook channel (future)\n    webhook_url: Optional[str] = None\n    \n    # Log channel (always on)\n    log_level: str = \"warning\"\n\n\nNOTIFICATION_CONFIG = {\n    \"log\": NotificationChannel(\n        name=\"structured-log\",\n        type=\"log\",\n        severity_filter=[\"info\", \"warning\", \"error\", \"critical\"],\n    ),\n    \"kafka\": NotificationChannel(\n        name=\"kafka-alerts\",\n        type=\"kafka\",\n        kafka_topic=\"osiris.alerts.critical\",\n        severity_filter=[\"warning\", \"critical\"],\n    ),\n    \"api\": NotificationChannel(\n        name=\"api-events\",\n        type=\"kafka\",\n        kafka_topic=\"osiris.events.platform\",\n        severity_filter=[\"info\", \"warning\", \"critical\"],\n    ),\n    # Future:\n    # \"pagerduty\": NotificationChannel(type=\"pagerduty\", ...)\n    # \"slack\": NotificationChannel(type=\"webhook\", webhook_url=\"https://hooks.slack.com/...\")\n}\n```\n\n### 7.4 Alert Output Schema\n\n```json\n{\n  \"alert_id\": \"alert_abc123def456\",\n  \"rule_name\": \"service_critical\",\n  \"severity\": \"critical\",\n  \"status\": \"firing\",\n  \"service_id\": \"osiris-data-postgres\",\n  \"group\": \"data\",\n  \"message\": \"osiris-data-postgres is CRITICAL (score=12)\",\n  \"health_score\": 12,\n  \"health_status\": \"critical\",\n  \"signals\": {\n    \"lifecycle\": 0,\n    \"http_health\": 0,\n    \"tcp_health\": 0,\n    \"dependency\": 50,\n    \"uptime\": 0,\n    \"latency\": 0,\n    \"error_rate\": 0\n  },\n  \"auto_action\": \"restart\",\n  \"auto_action_result\": \"pending\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-06-16T16:00:00Z\",\n  \"fired_at\": \"2026-06-16T16:00:00Z\",\n  \"acknowledged_at\": null,\n  \"resolved_at\": null,\n  \"escalation_level\": 1,\n  \"notification_channels\": [\"log\", \"kafka\"]\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## 8. Prometheus METRICS EXPORT\n\n```python\n# Metrics exported by the Health Scoring Engine\n\n# Per-service health score\nosiris_health_score{service=\"osiris-worker-ai\", group=\"worker\"} 95\nosiris_health_score{service=\"osiris-data-postgres\", group=\"data\"} 42\n\n# Per-signal breakdown\nosiris_health_signal{service=\"osiris-worker-ai\", signal=\"http_health\"} 100\nosiris_health_signal{service=\"osiris-worker-ai\", signal=\"latency\"} 90\n\n# Platform aggregate\nosiris_platform_health_score 87\nosiris_platform_availability_sli 0.88\nosiris_platform_error_budget_remaining 0.23\n\n# Service counts by status\nosiris_services_total{status=\"healthy\"} 22\nosiris_services_total{status=\"degraded\"} 1\nosiris_services_total{status=\"unhealthy\"} 1\nosiris_services_total{status=\"critical\"} 1\n\n# Alerts\nosiris_alerts_firing{severity=\"critical\"} 1\nosiris_alerts_firing{severity=\"warning\"} 2\nosiris_alerts_total{rule=\"service_critical\"} 15\n\n# Anomalies\nosiris_anomalies_detected{type=\"score_drop\"} 3\nosiris_anomalies_detected{type=\"oscillation\"} 1\n```\n\n---\n\n## 9.
